summary: 80-foot crow's nest in Lake County, Montana, dated to the 1920s and still in place in 2004; FFLA lists it as abandoned, not gone.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as a Crowsnest with status Abandoned; firelookout.com says it was still there in 2004

events.note: firelookout.com says the crow's nest was still there in 2004

evidence.supports: about 15 miles south of Swan Lake
lookout is in Lake County, Montana
FFLA lists a Crowsnest with status Abandoned
Swan Lake lies east of Flathead Lake and the town of Bigfork
evidence.quote: Swan Lake is a lake located east of Flathead Lake and the town of Bigfork, Montana

corrections.why: The FFLA Montana list gives Squeezer Creek the status Abandoned, not Gone. Firelookout.com says the crow's nest was still there in 2004, so it is not clearly gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says the crow's nest was still there in 2004 and gives no later date. The FFLA list marks it Abandoned with no date. Neither source says whether it still stands. The story reports both and does not call it standing or gone.

notes_for_editor: Two short lookout sources. firelookout.com gives the 1920s date and the 2004 presence note; the FFLA list gives the Crowsnest type, status Abandoned, and coordinates. Swan Lake's location is from Wikipedia, used only as a geographic reference. Not on the NHLR Montana list; FFLOS was not checked. Two web searches found nothing else on the site. The record's kind 'platform' may fit better as crowsnest per the FFLA list. Access and visit rules are unknown. The thin evidence keeps the story short.
